Ascanio Albertini was a Roman Catholic prelate who served as the Bishop of Avellino e Frigento from 1549 until his death in 1580. He was appointed Bishop on June 6, 1549, during the papacy of Pope Paul III. His tenure as bishop lasted for approximately 31 years. He succeeded Bartolomé de la Cueva y Toledo and was later succeeded by Pietrantonio Vicedomini.

The Diocese of Avellino e Frigento, located in Italy, is a Catholic ecclesiastical territory. Albertini's long service as bishop indicates he played a significant role in the religious and probably local matters of his diocese during the mid-16th century, a period that included the Counter-Reformation, following the Council of Trent.
